newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian withholding tax income disappoints govt.
newsitem.headline: Belgian withholding tax income disappoints govt.

text.p: Belgian withholding tax receipts from fixed income investments were disappointing in 1996, Finance Minister Philippe Maystadt said on Friday.
"Withholding tax receipts from fixed income investments at 60 billion (Belgian) francs were 21 percent lower than in the first eleven months of 1995," Maystadt told a news conference.
Maystadt said this fall, along with disappointing economic growth and overspending in the health sector, were the main reasons the government missed its 1996 deficit target.
The government said on Friday its 1996 deficit was around 3.4 percent of gross domestic product (GDP), compared with an original target of three percent.

Maystadt said withholding tax income probably fell because of the decline in long-term interest rates and an associated switch by the public to tax free investments, such as bank savings book accounts.
Belgium taxes interest on fixed income investments at 15 percent. Dividend income on equities is taxed at 25 percent.
Belgian investors greatly favour bonds and other fixed income investments over equities.
